intro: If you've been eyeing up that awkward bathroom in your Heriot cottage and thinking there has to be a better use of the space, a wet room could be exactly what you're looking for. Whether you're dealing with a compact Victorian-era bathroom that feels cramped around a traditional bath, or you simply want something more practical and stylish for everyday life, wet room installation has become one of the most popular bathroom upgrades in the area. Done properly, a wet room adds real value to a property and can transform how you start and end each day — no stepping over bath rims, no shower trays to clean around the edges, just a clean, open space that works.
localContext: Heriot sits in a quiet corner of Midlothian, and the housing stock here reflects that mix of Scottish rural character and more recent development. Older stone-built properties and period cottages make up a good portion of homes in and around the village, and these bring some specific considerations when it comes to wet room installation. Stone walls can be thick and irregular, which affects how waterproofing membranes are applied and how drainage channels are positioned. Floor joists in older properties may need assessment or reinforcement before a wet room former or screed can be laid safely. Modern estates in Heriot, on the other hand, tend to have more straightforward construction but may have tighter bathroom layouts that require careful planning. Heriot is also in a moderately hard water area, which is worth keeping in mind — limescale can build up on screen panels and fixtures, so choosing the right sealants and finishes at installation stage, and considering a scale-reducing shower head, will save you maintenance headaches down the line.
serviceDetail: A proper wet room installation in Heriot typically follows a clear sequence of work that takes between five and ten days depending on the scope. The first stage is stripping out the existing bathroom — removing the old suite, flooring, and any wall tiles. At this point a good installer will check the condition of the subfloor and walls before anything else goes in. For stone-built properties in Heriot this inspection stage really matters, as damp ingress or uneven substrates need addressing before waterproofing begins. The next stage is tanking — applying a waterproof membrane across the floor and walls. This is the most critical part of the job and should not be rushed. A sloped former or wet screed is then laid to ensure water drains efficiently toward the linear or point drain without pooling. Wall boards or tiles go on next, followed by the shower valve, fixed screen if desired, and all fixtures. Underfloor heating is often installed at the screed stage if you want it — and in a Heriot home that can get cold in winter, it's worth the modest additional cost. The final stage is grouting, sealing, and fitting sanitaryware before a full test of the drainage and water supply. A good installer will leave you with documentation of the waterproofing work completed.
pricing: In Heriot, wet room installation typically costs between £6,000 and £12,000 for a standard bathroom conversion. The lower end of that range usually applies to modern estate homes with straightforward construction and a smaller footprint. The higher end reflects older stone-built properties or period cottages where additional prep work is needed — reinforcing floors, managing damp, or working around irregular walls all add time and materials. Choosing premium fixtures, underfloor heating, or a bespoke drain position will push costs toward the top of the range. Always get a detailed written quote that separates labour from materials, and make sure waterproofing and waste work are explicitly included.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Heriot and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely makes a difference on a job like this. Someone familiar with the older stone-built properties here will know what to look for beneath the plaster and won't be surprised by the kind of quirks that come with period construction. Local trades also tend to have established relationships with regional suppliers, which can keep material lead times shorter. And if something needs revisiting after completion — a grout joint, a silicone seal — a local installer can come back without it becoming a logistical ordeal.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built property in Heriot?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires more preparation than a modern build. Stone walls need careful assessment for damp, and older floor structures may need reinforcing before the waterproof former or screed is laid. A qualified installer experienced with period properties in Heriot will factor this into their survey and quote from the outset, rather than discovering problems mid-job.

faqs.q: How does the moderately hard water in Heriot affect a wet room?
faqs.a: Limescale can leave marks on glass screens, chrome fittings, and tiled walls faster than in soft water areas. It's worth choosing a quality sealant on tiles, opting for a scale-reducing shower head, and keeping a squeegee handy for screens. Some homeowners in Heriot also install a small inline water softener on the shower supply to minimise buildup.

faqs.q: How long does wet room installation take in a typical Heriot home?
faqs.a: Most installations take between five and ten days from strip-out to completion. Simpler jobs in modern estate properties can come in at the lower end. Older stone-built or period cottage bathrooms in Heriot may take longer if additional floor prep, damp treatment, or bespoke drainage positioning is required. Your installer should give you a realistic programme before work starts.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a property in Heriot?
faqs.a: Generally yes, particularly in well-executed conversions with quality finishes. In a smaller village like Heriot where period cottages are common, a thoughtfully designed wet room can be a genuine selling point. Buyers looking for accessible, low-maintenance bathrooms respond well to them. A poorly waterproofed or cheaply finished wet room, however, can cause problems — so the quality of the installation matters enormously.
